newsitem.title: USA: U.S. sweet crudes deflated by West African glut.
newsitem.headline: U.S. sweet crudes deflated by West African glut.

text.p: U.S. sweet crude grades ended the week on a down note, paring differentials on sentiment the market is well-supplied at the current time.

"The market sees a lot of West African crude coming over," said an oil trader, noting Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James was sold at 18-20 cents premiums to the benchmark, some 5-10 cts weaker than late Thursday prices.

Sour grades remained steady for the most part, but have lost ground each session since April crude barrels became the prompt month on Tuesday. Apr West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was 60 cts off at $20.25-35 per barrel.
Outright price declines were based on NYMEX losses, which resulted from technical selling pushing April futures to the lowest spot month settlement in eight months.

News focused on Iraq, again, specifically on comments made early in the U.S. morning by Iraq's oil minister Amir Muhammad Rasheed that Baghdad would seek increased oil sales under the $2 billion oil-for-food accord.
Western diplomats at the United Nations doused that suggestion, saying there had been no request and raising the oil receipt income levels was out of the question.

For the cash markets, traders said the important fundamentals in the business are mostly on the bearish side. Sour prices have been under intense pressure with the new Iraqi crude offerings for the U.S. Gulf. Crude from Canada, South America and the West Coast are also competing for sales at a time of soft refinery demand, traders said.
West Texas Sour/Midland talked late in the session at WTI/Cushing -$2.40-50, selling prominently at a $2.44 and $2.45 discount to the benchmark.
Other trades heard in the market placed Eugene Island at $2.45 under the WTI/Cushing, 15 cts lower than Thursday.
Late widening in the Apr/May roll pushed Postings Plus to sell at $2.00 late in the afternoon, traders said.
Besides LLS, the other sweets were steady, with Midland/WTI sold at WTI/Cushing -37 cts and Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire discussed at a wide range from flat to 20 cts below WTI/Cushing.
